answer: A tide erases footprints, so standing must be re-earned every epoch. Each identity needs two holders outside its own juniper stand to countersign its mark, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one cooperative crew. Every mark is priced by rank: the k-th claim an operator files costs k squared in copper bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. An audit replays a random mark each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim clears the whole stand and forfeits its copper.
